growth.why_this_wins: Fresh 2026 neuroscience plus a universally understandable awake-versus-asleep paradox, with strong visual escalation through dolphins and flying birds and qualitative proof of audience curiosity.
growth.core_paradox: Sleep and wakefulness can coexist locally in the same brain instead of behaving as one global binary switch.
growth.hook_promise: Show how part of a brain can behave as if asleep while the organism remains awake, then escalate from a new 2026 experiment to dolphins, birds, and humans.
critic_lessons_applied: one major visual idea per beat
preserve scientific caveats without slowing the hook

research_questions: What exactly did the 2026 awake-mouse experiment induce and what cognitive benefit was measured?
What is local sleep and what evidence exists during wakefulness?
How does unihemispheric sleep work in dolphins and why is it adaptive?
What has been directly measured about sleep in flying frigatebirds?
What does the human first-night effect actually show, and what should not be overstated?
Could local sleep-like stimulation plausibly replace normal human sleep?
fact_risks: mouse result must not be presented as demonstrated in humans
humans must not be described as natural dolphin-style unihemispheric sleepers
local stimulation must not be presented as a replacement for normal sleep
